biography.plain_text: David J. Stern is an American former lawyer who built a large foreclosure practice in Plantation, Florida. A South Texas College of Law graduate, he founded his firm in 1994 after working for mortgage lenders. He also separated its associated nonlegal support operations into a publicly traded business, DJSP Enterprises.

long_biography.plain_text:
Former lawyer David J. Stern organised his business around the work that surrounded a foreclosure case: preparing documents, examining title and arranging sales of repossessed properties. Support staff and technology tracked cases from referral through completion, while he maintained relationships with the banks that supplied the work.

In 2010 he separated the nonlegal operations into a transaction with a public company that became DJSP Enterprises. He retained his law firm, which initially supplied all of the processing business's work, and became DJSP's chairman and chief executive. The deal paid cash and deferred consideration to Stern and his affiliated companies, while leaving them with an equity interest.

Identity is supported by exact-name professional reporting and two corresponding hull-name histories. Input ownership periods can precede a vessel's delivery; no relationship dates or vessel records are changed.

David Joel Stern, the late NBA commissioner, is a different person. Experity's chief executive, the German businessman, the psychotherapist and the California Savory Gourmet professional are not assigned to this owner.

Creation-sector materiality rests on personally owned services and realised economic benefits, not banks' mortgage assets or headline client volumes. The transaction's consideration included affiliated sellers, deferred amounts and equity; no aggregate is represented as his personal net worth.

The current-sector value is an explicit origin fallback. Historic residential and trust property is not enough to infer a presently dominant real-estate portfolio. A 2019 property-sale lead was only accessible as an indexed lead and was not used as decisive evidence.

Historical Founder is well supported but current Founder, Investor and Passive owner each lack a positive present principal-asset premise. Current relationship remains Unknown rather than assuming that sale proceeds were actively reinvested or exhausted.
Broad Self-made rests on an owned founder-built business after employment. Exact startup funding and material assistance are unestablished; neither narrow self-made subtype is inferred from silence.

Exact birth day, month and year are unverified. A reported age in 2010 cannot safely determine an exact birth year. An Illinois birthplace appears in derivative reporting but is withheld pending stronger primary corroboration. No secondary nationality is established.
